title: Fail-fast and fail-safe iterators
context: What do fail-fast and fail-safe mean for collection iterators?

source.title: JavaGuide (Snailclimb): Java collections questions (1 of 2)
source.note: Question and topic from this JavaGuide article. The answer is an original English write-up; see content/sources/javaguide/NOTICE.md.

answer: A fail-fast iterator, such as ArrayList's, checks a modification count. If the list changes during iteration outside the iterator, it throws ConcurrentModificationException on the next step. This is best-effort, not a guarantee. A fail-safe iterator, such as the one from CopyOnWriteArrayList or ConcurrentHashMap, works on a snapshot or tolerates changes, so it never throws, but it may not show the latest data. Remove items through the iterator's own remove method, or use removeIf.

points.title: ConcurrentModificationException
points.why: Changing a list inside a for-each loop throws on the next iteration step.

points.title: Safe removal
points.why: Use iterator.remove() or removeIf instead of list.remove inside a loop.
